\section[il salvataggio]{il salvataggio — the rescue}

\label{lesson:IT-C306-salvataggio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the avalanche, then the Italian for to drown.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il salvataggio}
\textbf{il salvataggio} — \textquotedblleft{}the rescue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il salvataggio è durato tutta la notte.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The rescue went on all night.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Il giubbotto di salvataggio} — the life jacket.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{salvataggio} is built on \emph{salvare} \textquotedblleft{}to save\textquotedblright{}, from Late Latin \emph{salvāre}, built on \emph{salvus} \textquotedblleft{}safe\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il salvataggio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il salvataggio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il salvataggio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the avalanche, then the Italian for to drown, then say \emph{il salvataggio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il salvataggio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The rescue\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il bagnino]{il bagnino — the lifeguard}

\label{lesson:IT-C306-bagnino}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to drown, then the Italian for the rescue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il bagnino}
\textbf{il bagnino} — \textquotedblleft{}the lifeguard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il bagnino ha salvato un bambino.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The lifeguard saved a child.}
\end{quote}

At the beach; a woman is \emph{la bagnina}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bagnino} is built on \emph{bagno} \textquotedblleft{}bath, bathing\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{balneum} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il bagnino}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il bagnino}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to drown, then the Italian for the rescue, then say \emph{il bagnino} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[il naufragio]{il naufragio — the shipwreck}

\label{lesson:IT-C306-naufragio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the rescue, then the Italian for the lifeguard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il naufragio}
\textbf{il naufragio} — \textquotedblleft{}the shipwreck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo il naufragio sono arrivati su un'isola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the shipwreck they reached an island.}
\end{quote}

Also a failure: \emph{il naufragio di un progetto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{naufragio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{naufragium} (EtymDB), built on \emph{nāvis} \textquotedblleft{}ship\textquotedblright{} and \emph{frangere} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il naufragio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il naufragio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the rescue, then the Italian for the lifeguard, then say \emph{il naufragio} again
\end{itemize}

\section[disperso]{disperso — missing (person)}

\label{lesson:IT-C306-disperso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the lifeguard, then the Italian for the shipwreck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disperso}
\textbf{disperso} — \textquotedblleft{}missing (person)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Due pescatori sono ancora dispersi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Two fishermen are still missing.}
\end{quote}

The past participle of \emph{disperdere}, ‘to scatter’.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disperso} is the past participle of \emph{disperdere} \textquotedblleft{}to scatter, to lose\textquotedblright{}; the form is usually traced to Latin \emph{dispersus}, the past participle of \emph{dispergere} \textquotedblleft{}to scatter\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disperso}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{disperso}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the lifeguard, then the Italian for the shipwreck, then say \emph{disperso} again

\section[sopravvivere]{sopravvivere — to survive}

\label{lesson:IT-C306-sopravvivere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the shipwreck, then the Italian for missing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sopravvivere}
\textbf{sopravvivere} — \textquotedblleft{}to survive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tutti sono sopravvissuti al naufragio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Everyone survived the shipwreck.}
\end{quote}

With \emph{essere}: \emph{è sopravvissuto}; \emph{sopravvivere a} — to survive something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sopravvivere} joins \emph{sopra} \textquotedblleft{}over\textquotedblright{} and \emph{vivere} \textquotedblleft{}to live\textquotedblright{}, modelled on Latin \emph{supervīvere} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sopravvivere}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sopravvivere}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sopravvivere}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the shipwreck, then the Italian for missing, then say \emph{sopravvivere} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
